item.title: Scale E Agent in North West Agency, 23-month opportunity
item.description: Location: Manchester The Bank of England Agency Network The Bank’s Agents are the representatives of the Bank of England in the twelve Agencies across the English regions and Devolved Nations. The Agencies are the ‘eyes, ears and voice’ of the Bank in their respective parts of the United Kingdom. Agents play a crucial role in informing the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) and the Financial Policy Committee’s (FPC) assessment of the economic and financial environment through gathering, analysing, and reporting economic intelligence from regular meetings with their network of contacts. Agents talk to senior contacts from a wide range of organisations – from small businesses to large global companies – across all sectors of the economy, to gain an insight into how businesses are operating and their future plans. This provides a unique perspective into how the real economy is evolving and the factors driving those developments. The Agents also communicate policymakers’ core messages to business contacts and other local audiences across the UK. This includes regular presentations on the Monetary Policy Report and Financial Stability Report to support a widespread understanding and trust of the monetary and financial policy framework. Agents also coordinate interactions and host meetings between policymakers and their local contacts, so that they can hear the views of businesses and communities first-hand. Job Description Carries out external engagement within The North West of England and, on occasion, across the North East and Yorkshire and the Humber with the principal aim of gathering intelligence and carrying out representational functions for the key policy functions of the Bank of England. Works as part of a team on a technical Area of Expertise (AoE), led by a Technical Agent, to construct an economic narrative and/or strategy, contributing to policy analysis, discussion and decision making. The Area of Expertise for this role, which may change over time, will be employment, pay and capacity utilisation. Agents, as part of their AoE team, analyse and summarise qualitative intelligence to bring an ongoing, timely narrative to the policy discussion. Agents as part of a rota can lead the analysis and present to the MPC during a policy round with the support of the lead Technical Agent and AoE team. Agents work on specific projects assigned to Working Groups and may lead on specific projects and matrix manage other members of the Working Group. Agents will work closely with the Senior Data Scientist and the Data team to trial and implement new tools and analytical approaches. Scale E Agents can expect to undertake rotating secondments to other parts of the Bank or work on structured joint analytical projects, to broaden their knowledge, expertise and networks in the Bank. Reports to: The scale D Managing Agent for the North of England (currently Alex Golledge) Location: Needs to live in, or very close to, the North West region. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria Experience in summarising qualitative information into reports for use by decision makers Experience in communicating effectively with senior business people An understanding of and interest in economics and/or economic policy Essential criteria: Demonstrate an understanding of the Bank’s approach to monetary policy and its policy framework more generally. A good communicator, comfortable interacting with senior external contacts. Ability to learn quickly, work independently and deliver good quality outputs to agreed timetables. Able to work collaboratively with colleagues within and/or outside the Bank. Desirable criteria: Experience of conducting interviews to gather qualitative data. Experience of delivering presentations to diverse audiences and explaining complex messages clearly and concisely. A full driving licence. A degree in economics or equivalent work experience Travel is an essential part of the role. A car allowance and mileage payment are paid to the role holder to facilitate this. This role requires a combination of in-person meetings and virtual meetings with Agency contacts in the North West and, occasionally, elsewhere in the North of England. It also requires regular in-person meetings with the Agency team in Manchester and with the other teams in the North of England in Leeds. There are also occasional meetings with UK-wide colleagues in London and Leeds. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. The salary range for this role is, Manchester: £72,720 - £81,810. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two interview stages. (Amend and add brief details if relevant, such as interview/assessment dates or process for your specific role) This role closes on: 11 September 2026. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Head of Workplace and Estates
item.description: The FCA has retained Odgers to look after this role on our behalf. The following link will take you to the Odgers website where you will be able to apply www.odgers.com/96619 About the FCA At the FCA, we’re creating a fair and more resilient financial system. We’re establishing more transparent relationships between financial services and customers, building trust in financial markets and protecting vulnerable consumers. We’re currently on an exciting journey as we drive forward significant organisational, people, process, and technology transformation to become a more forward-thinking, proactive regulator. We will use data more effectively to drive better regulatory decisions and build greater cohesion across our broad financial services remit. Significant improvements in digital enablement, business intelligence, market data and information management maturity are all being pursued to maintain our position as a world leader in financial services regulation. In March 2025, the FCA launched a new 5-year strategy to deepen trust, rebalance risk, support growth and improve lives. The FCA will focus on four priorities: Be a smarter regulator ; predictable, purposeful and proportionate. The FCA will improve its processes and embrace technology to become more efficient and effective. Support sustained economic growth , by enabling investment, innovation and ensuring the continued competitiveness of the UK’s world-leading financial services. Help consumers navigate their financial lives by working with industry to boost trust, product innovation and ensuring the right information and support is available for people to take financial decisions. Fight financial crime , focusing on those who seek to use the fact they are regulated to do harm. It will go further to disrupt criminals and support firms to be an effective line of defence. The Role The FCA has a workforce of 5,500 spread across three sites in London, Edinburgh, and Leeds. London is the largest office with approximately 4,800 staff located in 12 Endeavour Square. We have committed to continued growth outside of London and have also adopted hybrid working practices. There is a small in-house team with the majority of services outsourced under two key contracts. The team sits within the Operations Division and the Finance & Corporate Services Directorate, reporting to the Director of Finance. This role will lead the team, oversee our contracts, and ensure the FCA is getting maximum value from its estate. The building and services are key to our staff and our employment offer and maintaining a high level of excellence is key. There are also opportunities to evolve the offering as hybrid working practices become clearer, technologies advance and our ways of working change. What will the candidate get from the role? Providing strategic direction and leadership for a team of Facilities, Estates, Security and H&S professionals in relatively new buildings. Managing a significant budget and contractual relationships Opportunity to develop and evolve space in line with changing working practices Be part of an organisation that plays a significant part in protecting consumers and our economy Key responsibilities: Lead the team with overall responsibility for Estates, Facilities, Corporate Security and Health & Safety. This includes all aspects of setting overall direction, objectives and measuring performance and key trends. The facilities being overseen include front of house, security, cleaning, gym, staff restaurant and AV. Management of the relationships with both our superior landlord and a significant tenant that the FCA subleases to. Overseeing key suppliers who deliver our services to ensure compliance, value and the highest quality of service. Ensuring the estate is resilient, has adequate contingency plans and running disaster recovery responses where necessary Ensuring the organisation has the right space design and planning to continue effectively meeting its objectives . Ensuring our estate delivers against our sustainability goals. Developing and delivering a long-term strategy for the department , aligning to broader divisional and organisational strategies Leading on performance, capability, and culture within the department , with a strong focus on operational excellence Building a strong and inclusive directorate that attracts and develop diverse talent. Skills/Experience Required We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. (To learn more about the Disability Confident Scheme Click Here ) Minimum Strong experience of managing a facilities, estates, and infrastructure team Strong leadership capabilities - a role model for the Estates & Facilities team with the ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams through change. Extensive experience of managing outsourced Facilities Management supplier contracts Experience of estate planning, space planning and running projects Essential Extensive experience of managing a facilities operation in a corporate workplace Experience of managing relationships with both landlord and managing significant tenants Strong experience of health & safety management Strong experience of physical security risk assessment and management Responsibility for keeping leased building in operation and maintaining its condition Ability to get the best out of suppliers working in partnership with others across the FCA Confident, assertive and able to influence and challenge stakeholders Desirable Operating in a high rise, high quality office estate Estate transactions NEBOSH qualification The FCA’s Values & Diversity Our ambition is to create a diverse and inclusive workplace that reflects the society we serve, helping us to be a better regulator. We serve the public and our decisions directly affect the wellbeing of people, businesses and the UK economy. So, our values matter. They represent the culture we aspire to every day, guiding our judgements, building trust and helping us to be ‘At our best ’. The FCA is committed to achieving greater diversity across all levels of our organisation. Given this, we particularly welcome applications from women, disabled, and minority ethnic candidates, as under-represented groups. As an inclusive employer, we are open to considering flexible working arrangements, including job shares. Please inform your recruiter if you wish to apply for this role on a flexible basis. Application Support We want to remove any possible barriers and are committed to providing a wide range of reasonable adjustments so that you can keep the focus on your conversations and be at your best. If you have an accessibility requirement, disability, or condition that means you might require changes to the recruitment process, please contact your recruiter to discuss this further. Our aim is to make you application as easy as possible, and your recruiter will be happy to work with you to make any necessary arrangements where possible. Benefits Our competitive benefits scheme gives you the opportunity to create a personalised benefits package, tailored to suit your lifecycle. You can this this allowance to purchase additional benefits such as dental or cycle to work, or you have the option to top up your base salary by taking this as cash. Core benefits that you will receive as standard are: 30 days holiday per year plus bank holidays Private healthcare with Bupa A non-contributory Pension of at least 8% of basic salary each month (there are several contribution levels that increase depending on your age- up to 12% a month once you reach age 35) Life assurance of eight times your basic salary Income protection Conflicts of interest All applicants to the FCA are required to demonstrate that they do not have other interests likely to conflict with their responsibilities as an employee of the FCA. You should declare any potential conflict of interest as early as possible in the selection process, and also disclose information or personal connections that, if appointed, might be open to misperception. Any potential conflicts of interest will not prevent candidates going forward to interview but may, if appropriate , be explored during the interview to establish how the candidate would address the issue(s) should they be successful in their application. Useful information The closing date for this role is 23:55 on Sunday 20 September Selection will be via a two-stage interview and psychometric assessment If successful, you will be required to obtain and retain SC Clearance. From September 2026, FCA employees will be required to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office. Our Executive Director and Directors will be expected to be in a minimum of 60% per month. The salary range for the role is £1 30 , 0 00- £150,000 This role will be London based only To apply please submit your CV and cover letter , using this link www.odgers.com/96619 The FCA has retained Odgers to look after this role on our behalf. The following link will take you to the Odgers website where you will be able to apply www.odgers.com/96619 If you have any questions regarding your application, please contact Peter Lawrence on Peter.Lawrence@odgers.com

item.title: Senior Associate – Market Research Manager
item.description: Job Title: Senior Associate – Market Research M anager Division : Supervision , Policy and Competition Directorate: Cross Cutting Policy & Strategy Department : Cross-Cutting Response, Research & Contracts Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £67,199 and London £59,200 to £73,799 per annum (Salary offered will b e based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your recruitment contact is: Louis Van den Burg via Louis.vandenburg@fca.org.uk Your External Recruitment contact is : Tahir Kahn via Tahir.Khan1@fca.org.uk Application must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. You will need a CV and a supporting statement no longer than 500 words . T he supporting statement is mandatory . Applications without a covering letter may not be accepted . We are also advertising for a Research Specialist ( JR0022287 ). You can apply for both roles through one application . Please indicate in your supporting statement if you are interested in, and why you are suitable for, both roles . About the FCA and the team The FCA regulates the conduct of c 3 5 , 5 00 firms in the UK to ensure our financial markets are honest, fair and competitive. Follow this link to find out more About the FCA . The FCA’s Market Research team provides vital consumer insights that support regulatory decisions. They deliver the Financial Lives survey (FLS) – a key, nationally representative study tracking UK consumer s’ attitudes, behaviours and financial experiences. The team also conducts bespoke surveys and qualitative research for other areas of the FCA, collaborates with third-party data providers and ensures consumer insights are embedded across the organisation. Their work informs policy, identifies emerging issues and measures regulatory impact – helping to keep the consumer voice central to financial oversight. The team also ma nages a smaller amount of firm research, inc ludin g res earch about the perce ptions firm s an d ot her sta kehol der s have of the FCA and how fir ms exper ience r egu latio n . Role r esponsibilities The role will be around 50 % on FLS, and around 5 0 % on bespoke research , focused on research management . You will work closely with the team leads (Lead Associates) for FLS and for Bespoke research. You will e nsur e FLS is delivered to time and budget through excellent timetabling , coordinating dependencies across workstreams and suppliers , resource allocation, progress monitoring , supplier manage ment and stakeholder engagement . This will include w orking wi th the t eam t o man age respon ses to the many queries we receive for FLS analysis in FCA papers and publications . It will al so inclu de mana ging the MI ( ma nagemen t informa tion ) we col lect on the types of queries we rec e ive and from w hich p art s of the b usiness . Yo u will also manag e the internal governance processes to sign off FLS publications . Contracts are in place with 4 agencies for FLS up till wave 7 ending in 2031. You will manage the FLS budget spreadsheet, liaise with suppliers monthly to agree invoice amounts and produce a monthly summary for Finance. You will also produce forecasts as required by Finance . FLS runs on a 2 year cycle, meaning that every 2 years you will manage the process of reagreeing scope and costs with suppliers for the upcoming wave. Within each 2-year wave, you will manage contract variations, as needed . You will also provide project management support for the procurement and delivery of bespoke market research projects , through excellent timetabling, resource allocation, progress monitoring, supplier management and stakeholder engagement . An important task will be to help build and maintain the pipeline of work coming into the team . We have a Market Research Framework in place, to source suppliers – th is will be renewed in 2028, and you will have a sub stant ial role in planning this renewal from around mid 2027 . There is an option for you to run smaller bespoke projects, ie working on the research it self ( eg design , analysis and r eporting) , s ubject to your availability and interests . You will also support stakeholder engagement and communications planning to maximise the value of all the Market Research Team’s outputs , helping to ensur e they are embedded in publications, speeches, policy development, supervision work and strategic decision-making. Finally, you will c ontribute to w ider team management , including recruitment coordination, man a ging the agendas for team meetings and heredays , updating FCA systems about the data we hold and any risks we own, and continuous improvement of Market Research Team processes and record-keeping . Skills Required Minimum Prior experience managing market research projects within a market research agency , regulator or government department , including devising and overseeing workstreams and detailed timelines as well as overseeing suppliers . Strong organisational skills, with the ability to work autonomously and del iver on your ow n ini tiati ve , to manage competing priorities, to work collaboratively to ac hieve wider tea m goals , and to keep delivery on track. High attention to detail, with the ability to implement and maintain processes that ensure the quality and rigour of the team’s work . Essential Good knowledge of a broad range of quantitative and qualitative research methodologies , with e xperience in survey design, questionnaire development, and analysis and reporting. With these skills, you will be able to help the team create and keep to workable projects and project timelines . Ability to manage complex timelines and capacity plans ( eg using Gantt charts and Excel) , adapting delivery to changing priorities, resource constraints and competing demands . Excellent team-working skills to support the team and help them to manage their own resource and priorities . Strong stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to engage senior colleagues, subject matter experts, operational teams and suppliers . Experience of managing research budgets , with a high level of ability in Excel for this . Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Hybrid model where employees currently work a minimum of 5 0% in the office each month A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes , we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. item.title: Senior Associate – Market Research specialist
item.description: Job Title: Senior Associate – Market R esearch specialist Division : Supervision , Policy and Competition Directorate: Cross Cutting Policy & Strategy Department : Cross-Cutting Response, Research & Contracts Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £67,199 and London £59,200 to £73,799 per annum (Salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your recruitment contact is: Louis Van den Burg via Louis.vandenburg@fca.org.uk Your External Recruitment contact is : Tahir Kahn via Tahir.Khan1@fca.org.uk Application must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. You will need a CV and a supporting statement no longer than 500 words . T he supporting statement is mandatory . P l ease i nclude links to an y research publ icatio ns. Applications without a covering letter may not be accepted . We are also advertising for a Research Manager ( JR0022259 ). You can apply for both roles through one application . Please indicate in your supporting statement if you are interested in, and why you are suitable for, both roles . About the FCA and the team The FCA regulates the conduct of c 3 5 , 5 00 firms in the UK to ensure our financial markets are honest, fair and competitive. Follow this link to find out more About the FCA . The FCA’s Market Research team provides vital consumer insights that support regulatory decisions. The team conducts bespoke surveys and qualitative research for other areas of the FCA, collaborates with third-party data providers and ensures consumer insights are embedded across the organisation. They also deliver the Financial Lives survey (FLS) – a key, nationally representative study tracking UK consumer s’ attitudes, behaviours and financial experiences. Their work informs policy, identifies emerging issues and measures regulatory impact – helping to keep the consumer voice central to financial oversight. The tea m also ma nages a smaller amount of firm research, inc ludin g res earch about the perce ptions firm s an d ot her sta kehol der s have of the FCA and how fir ms exper ience r egu latio n . Role r esponsibilities The role will be around 75% on bespoke research and around 25% on FLS . You will work closely with the team leads (Lead Associates) for FLS and for Bespoke research. You will work with our internal clients, to write excellent Statements of Requirements ( SoRs ) for new bespoke research , assess/ evaluate agency bids, and work with appointed suppliers to ensure research projects are delivered on time and within budget. You will be responsible for ensuring that projects use optimal data collection , data is robust, and findings are analysed and reported well. For quantitative bespoke projects you will ensure that sampling, screening and weigh t ing are addressed as early as needed in the project timeline, and that outputs will meet client needs . For qual itative research you will ensure pro jects meet client needs , wh ether they are standalone projects , or intended to help design a survey or to fill the gaps quantitative research cannot fill, or to inform be havioural testing research run by our colleagues in Economics. For some projects, you r role may be to design the survey or t he qualitat ive research , and/or to provide in a SoR a clear research design for agencies to refine. So met imes y ou wi ll produc e a first draft o f the questi onnai re or discuss ion guide . You will be responsible for two or three of the retail financial sectors or topics covered by the FLS, meaning you deliver the questionnaire, the tabspec and the slides-based report for these sections of the survey. Strong organisational skills, with the ability to work autonomously and del iver on your ow n ini tiati ve , to manage competing priorities, to work collaboratively to ac hieve wider tea m goals , and to keep delivery on track. High attention to detail, with the ability to implement and maintain processes that ensure the quality and rigour of the team’s work . Essential Experience of designing and conducting research for, or on behalf of, a financial services organisation or a public sector organisation . Very good knowledge of a broad range of quantitative and qualitative research methodologies, with the ability to analyse results effectively . Experience of writing reports to publication standard, in PowerPoint and in Word . Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Broad understanding of the different retail sectors within the financial services industry and the regulatory environment in which it operates , E xperience of designing and conducting research in one or more financial services sectors ( or an ability to demonstrate you will get up to speed quickly ) . item.title: Lead Delivery Engineer
item.description: Lead Delivery Engineer, Technology Directorate Location - Leeds Permanent Full Time Flexible Working Options: This role is open to flexible working patterns. These may include: Flexible start and end time to each day. Ability to adapt calendar as needed, for example to fit in the school run, gym or appointments. A 50% in-office attendance requirement that can be spread across the month to accommodate diverse working patterns, such as the flexibility to purchase a weekly train ticket for certain weeks. Working from abroad policy, subject to approval and policy within the team. The Technology Directorate provides information and system technology services to all business areas in the Bank as part of Central Services. Our key objective is to support the policy and operational divisions to meet the Bank’s stated objectives. An exciting opportunity has arisen for an Azure and M365 Specialist to join the Digital Workplace team. This role will work as part of the wider Microsoft 365 team within Digital Workplace, a function responsible for delivering and supporting the collaboration, productivity and information management services used across the Bank. The team owns and supports core Microsoft 365 services including SharePoint, Teams, Copilot, and related information governance capabilities, alongside specialist information management and preservation platforms. We want to make more of the technology that we have and explore opportunities to use it in new ways to make the Bank more effective. The successful candidate will bring Azure cloud experience to help design, implement and support automation solutions, service integrations and technical improvements across Microsoft 365 technologies and services. The role combines technical problem solving, stakeholder engagement, cloud engineering and continual service improvement, while contributing to the wider evolution of Digital Workplace services. This is an ideal role for someone who enjoys learning new technologies, working closely with business stakeholders, and improving services that deliver long-term organisational value. A typical day could start with a sprint stand-up with the wider team, checking progress against current priorities and agreeing how to unblock delivery. You might then join project meetings with stakeholders, take part in solution design conversations with technical colleagues, or raise change requests for product or service changes. At lunch time, you could head over to the office canteen to have a break with your colleagues, then head to an event organised by an employee network. For the second half of the day, you might be investigating incidents impacting the team’s Azure-hosted solutions, troubleshooting service issues and identifying improvements to prevent recurrence. Finally, you might dedicate some time to review upcoming changes from Microsoft to identify risks and opportunities. Key Responsibilities • Design and implement best practice Azure-based solutions that integrate with core Microsoft 365 products to improve business processes and information management outcomes. • Support Azure-hosted services and manage associated cloud resources used by the wider Digital Workplace team. • Investigate, troubleshoot and resolve technical incidents, problems and service requests at a third line level. • Document technical solutions, support procedures and operational processes. • Share knowledge with colleagues and contribute to the development of technical capability within the wider team. • Identify opportunities to improve service reliability, supportability, automation and user experience. Minimum Criteria • Experience supporting, administering or implementing Microsoft Azure cloud solutions in an enterprise environment, including services that integrate with Microsoft 365 technologies. • Experience administering core Microsoft 365 services such as SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business and Teams. • Ability to gather requirements, assess service improvement opportunities and independently design practical technical solutions that improve supportability, automation or user experience. • Strong troubleshooting, documentation and communication skills, with experience supporting business-critical services and working effectively across technical and business teams. Essential Criteria • A proactive approach to service improvement and knowledge sharing. • Awareness of how information governance, records management, compliance and data lifecycle principles influence the design and operation of workplace technology services. • Ability to build effective working relationships with stakeholders, suppliers and technical teams, translating needs into practical, well-governed outcomes. • Strong analytical judgement, with the ability to understand complex issues, evaluate options and recommend proportionate solutions. • Technical curiosity and learning agility, with enthusiasm for exploring new technologies, building knowledge independently and acting as a trailblazer for emerging capabilities. • A continuous improvement mindset, with the confidence to challenge existing ways of working and help shape better, more sustainable service outcomes. Desirable Criteria • Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio or AI Foundry, including exploring practical use cases for AI-enabled productivity, automation or service improvement. • Power Platform technologies, particularly Power Automate and Power Apps, to deliver low-code automation and business process improvements. • APIs, automation technologies, systems integration or Infrastructure as Code and DevOps tooling. • Microsoft Purview, information governance, records management, document management, archival or digital preservation systems. • Working in a regulated, public sector or highly governed environment, including effective engagement with third-party suppliers. • Plus, any relevant Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Copilot or Power Platform certifications. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Leeds Salary: £49,360 - £55,530 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application ques

item.title: Enforcement Investigator
item.description: Job Title: Enforcement Investigator Division: Enforcement & Market Oversight Department : Retail and Regulatory Investigations Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £47,200 to £62,900 and London from £50,300 to £67,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Associate – Level 8 - Practising Legal For Internal candidates, your recruitment contact is Rhianna via rhianna.walkden@fca.org.uk For External candidates, your recruitment contact is Riley via riley.fox@fca.org.uk . Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. Enforcement & Market Oversight (EMO) is responsible for the FCA’s responsibilities for market monitoring, delivery of the functions of the UK Listing Authority (UKLA) and the investigation and prosecution of misconduct using the whole spectrum of criminal, civil and administrative sanctions and remedies against firms and individuals. Retail and Regulatory Investigations (RRI) investigates potential misconduct by regulated firms and individuals working within those firms, involved in retail banking, stockbroking, asset management, mortgage broking and lending, insurance intermediation, financial advice, consumer credit and payment services. We take action against firms that sell unsuitable products or services to consumers, mishandle client money and assets, or have governance and systemic issues. We also investigate financial crime matters including fraud and misconduct related to AML systems and controls. Role responsibilities Associates are involved at every stage of the investigation process, supporting your team, developing your knowledge and sharing your experience, which includes: Taking on differing degrees of responsibility for a mixture of cases depending on their nature and complexity. This could range from playing a leading role in smaller cases with management oversight, to working as part of a wider team on larger more complex cases Progressing a portfolio of investigations, managing your work to meet competing deadlines. Obtaining evidence through the use of appropriate tools and powers and developing the case team’s understanding. Exploring detailed evidence and making recommendations Drafting all forms of case documents (which may include witness statements, civil orders, statutory notices and papers going before the Regulatory Decision Committee) and correspondence with investigation subjects, their legal representatives and witnesses Participating in challenging interviews of subjects and witnesses using compulsory powers, on a voluntary basis and under caution Preparing for and presenting cases at, internal case committees when required Where appropriate, provide legal advice to the case team and where appropriate take responsibility for the preparation of privileged correspondence Skills required Minimum: Prior experience of analysing large amounts of information and producing summaries which make conclusions and draw out key findings You must hold a valid practising certificate issued by the Solicitors Regulation Authority for England and Wales (if a solicitor), or the General Council of the Bar for England and Wales (if a barrister) (or a similar internationally recognised qualification) Essential: Demonstrated experience supporting and progressing investigations or complex projects involving large volumes of information Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including in challenging or sensitive contexts Experience working collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams and managing competing priorities across multiple workstreams Clear written and verbal communication skills, including producing clear, structured written outputs and presenting findings or recommendations Relevant experience in financial services and/or fraud investigation/litigation Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values & culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability Confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timeline Advert Closing: 6th September at 11:59pm CV Review/Shortlist: 8th September Interviews: w/c 21st September Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time.

item.title: Technical Product Manager (DevOps)
item.description: Technical Product Manager (DevOps), Technology Directorate Location: Leeds or London Permanent Full Time Job Description RTGS is the Bank of England's Real Time Gross Settlement service, critical national infrastructure that underpins the UK financial system, settling hundreds of billions of pounds each day. We are looking for a Technical Product Manager to help shape and evolve the platform services that enable software delivery across RTGS Technology. Working within the Runtime Platform & Developer Experience domain, you will own the roadmap, epics, backlog and demand management processes for the engineering platforms and services that enable software delivery across RTGS Technology. You will work closely with engineers, architects, Software Engineering Team Leads and stakeholders to understand platform needs, shape demand and ensure platform capabilities evolve in line with technology strategy, engineering priorities, lifecycle obligations and operational requirements. This role sits at the intersection of platform engineering, software delivery and product management. You will own a balanced roadmap that ensures platform services remain secure, resilient, supportable and fit for the future. Working with engineers and stakeholders, you will prioritise demand, reduce operational toil through automation, manage technology lifecycle obligations and improve the effectiveness of software delivery across RTGS Technology. Acting as a steward of engineering capacity, you will help maintain a sustainable delivery model that balances operational responsibilities, platform evolution and continuous improvement. This is an opportunity to shape the future of engineering platforms within RTGS Technology and help enable the delivery of one of the UK's most critical technology services. Flexible Working Options This role is open to flexible working patterns, these may include: Flexible start and end time to each day Ability to adapt calendar as needed, this could be to fit in the school run, gym, or appointments A 50% in-office attendance requirement can be spread across the month to accommodate diverse working patterns, such as the flexibility to purchase a weekly train ticket for certain weeks Working from abroad policy (subject to approval and policy within the team) A Day in the Role One day you could be working with engineering teams to understand challenges within the software delivery lifecycle and identify opportunities to improve platform capabilities and engineering effectiveness. You may be working with Software Engineering Team Leads, architects and stakeholders to review roadmap priorities, balance competing demands and make informed trade-offs across platform improvements, lifecycle management, resilience, automation and operational support. At the same time, you could be working with platform engineers to prioritise upgrades, patching activities, technology refresh, obsolescence remediation and operational improvements, ensuring the team maintains the right balance between supporting today's services and investing in tomorrow's platform. No two days will be the same, but the focus remains consistent: maintaining a sustainable roadmap, evolving platform capabilities and enabling engineering teams to deliver software safely, efficiently and at scale. Role Requirements You will be responsible for translating engineering needs, operational requirements and technology priorities into a coherent and sustainable roadmap for Runtime Platform & Developer Experience services. Own the creation, maintenance and ongoing evolution of the roadmap, epics and backlog for Runtime Platform & Developer Experience services. Work closely with engineering teams and platform consumers to understand needs, identify opportunities for improvement and shape platform priorities through workshops, discovery activities and collaborative planning. Ensure engineering capacity is allocated appropriately across platform evolution, lifecycle management, operational support, resilience, automation and continuous improvement activities. Use feedback, operational insights and service data to identify bottlenecks, inform prioritisation decisions and drive continuous improvement. Maintain a balanced roadmap that supports platform reliability, lifecycle management, resilience, automation, developer experience and continuous improvement. Drive lifecycle management activities including patching, upgrades and obsolescence remediation whilst identifying opportunities to reduce operational effort through automation and standardisation. Work closely with Software Engineering Team Leads, architects and platform engineers to shape future platform direction. Challenge demand that could lead to unsustainable delivery or compromise long-term platform health. Communicate priorities, risks, dependencies and outcomes to stakeholders. Minimum Criteria We’re looking for someone who has the following key skills and experience: Experience managing roadmaps, backlogs, epics or prioritisation processes within a technology organisation. Experience working with engineering, technology or platform teams. Experience facilitating workshops, discovery activities or stakeholder engagement sessions. Experience improving operational processes, engineering effectiveness or service outcomes. Strong stakeholder management and communication skills. Understanding of Agile delivery and product management practices. Essential Criteria We are interested in hearing from candidates who have the following capabilities: Proven experience as a Product Manager, Technical Product Manager, Platform Product Manager or similar role within a technology environment. Experience owning roadmaps, epics and backlogs for technical products, platforms or services. Experience working within a software -or platform engineering environment. Strong understanding of software delivery, CI/CD, developer tooling, platform engineering concepts and modern engineering practices. Experience working closely with engineering teams, architects and technical stakeholders. Experience facilitating workshops and collaborative discovery activities. Experience defining and prioritising platform capabilities based on user needs, operational requirements and strategic objectives. Experience using feedback, operational insights and adoption data to shape roadmap decisions. Experience balancing platform evolution, lifecycle obligations, resilience, operational requirements and engineering productivity. Experience managing or prioritising work relating to platform lifecycle management, technology obsolescence, patching, upgrades or operational resilience. Strong planning, facilitation and stakeholder management skills. Ability to understand technical concepts and translate them into prioritised outcomes. Strong communication skills and ability to influence technical and non-technical stakeholders. Desirable Criteria It would also be beneficial, but not necessary, to have some of the following: Experience improving software delivery processes or engineering productivity. Experience using techniques such as value stream mapping, process mapping, journey mapping or similar approaches to identify improvement opportunities. Experience driving automation and operational efficiency initiatives. Experience with cloud and on-premise platform environments. Experience in financial services, payments or regulated environments. Knowledge of operational resilience, observability and technology lifecycle management practices. Don't hesitate to apply if you don't meet all the essential criteria. We value diverse perspectives and believe that different backgrounds can contribute to our team's success. How This Role Fits into the Wider Bank RTGS Technology is undergoing a significant transformation, moving to a product engineering model with teams aligned to business and platform domains. The Technical Product Manager reports to the Technology Product Lead and forms part of the Product Management function within RTGS Technology. This role exists to ensure RTGS engineering teams have secure, reliable and sustainable platform services that enable them to develop, deploy and operate software efficiently whilst maintaining long-term platform health and operational resilience. The Technical Product Manager owns the roadmap, epics and backlog for Runtime Platform & Developer Experience services, ensuring demand is prioritised and engineering capacity is directed towards the highest-value outcomes. Success in this role will be measured through improvements in engineering effectiveness, operational resilience, successful lifecycle management, reduction in manual effort through automation and the maintenance of a sustainable delivery model that enables continuous improvement without compromising operational stability. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. item.title: Senior Policy Advisor
item.description: Job title: Senior Policy Advisor Division: Supervision, Policy and Competition (SPC) Department: Cross-Cutting Policy Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £63,500 and London from £59,200 to £67,000 (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your internal recruitment contact is Louis Van Den Burg via louis.vandenburg@fca.org.uk Your external recruitment contact is Tahir Khan via tahir.khan1@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). Sitting within Cross-Cutting Policy & Strategy (CCPS), the Fees Policy team is responsible for developing and maintaining the FCA’s policy framework for recovering its costs. Our work is central to the operation of the FCA, requiring us to balance strategic, regulatory and operational considerations while working closely with stakeholders across the organisation and industry. Through our policy framework, we determine how the FCA funds its activities, ensuring that it remains sustainable and proportionate. Role responsibilities Own key policy projects, drawing on solid methodical, stakeholder management and project management skills Lead delivery of the team's core programme of work, including the annual fees cycle, managing multiple workstreams to ensure high-quality outcomes Develop evidence-based policy proposals and present recommendations to senior decision-makers across the FCA Build productive working relationships with stakeholders across the FCA to drive policy development and implementation Represent the FCA externally with government departments, including the Treasury as well as industry participants, trade bodies and other regulators Tackle complex fees policy questions, using sound judgement to develop and advance policy thinking Skills required Minimum: Demonstrated policy experience within financial services or other regulatory environments Experience in building constructive working relationships with internal and external stakeholders at all levels Experience preparing papers, publications and briefings for senior audiences Essential: Demonstrated ability to lead complex projects, navigate governance processes effectively and deliver high-quality work at pace Solid analytical skills, with the ability to analyse complex information and develop proposals for new policies and approaches Experience of working effectively as part of a team, supporting others to reach shared goals and adjusting your approach as circumstances require Capability to identify and manage key internal and external stakeholders, with the experience to engage with, question, and work constructively with them Demonstrated ability to communicate persuasively and credibly, explaining complex issues succinctly and clearly to audiences less familiar with the subject matter Sound judgement, well-developed attention to detail and the ability to work flexibly and on your own initiative with minimal supervision Effective organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to deliver multiple tasks and workstreams when deadlines are tight and within challenging timeframes Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Hybrid model where employees work a minimum of 50% in the office each month (expectation of 60% for Directors and Executive Directors) A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim ton find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. item.title: Data Security Assurance Lead
item.description: D ata Security Assurance Lead Division: Operations Department: Cyber and Information Resilience Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £57,000 to £77,000 and London from £63,000 to £85,000. (Salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Lead Associate, Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Raimonda via raimonda.stankute@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Fizah via fizahfarouk.ibrahim@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth and shaping the future of UK finance services. Cyber and Information Resilience (C&IR) is responsible for the management of cyber security at the FCA. 'Cyber security' means the protection of the FCA's data and systems from malicious activity, including theft, damage and disruption, in order that the FCA can deliver its key business functions. C&IR is now part of a new formed Directorate lead by our CISO, Director of Cyber & Operational Resilience Division. ​​​​​​The role is based in the Cyber Assurance team, who leads on the FCA & PSR cyber assurance activities working to determine that correct cyber assurance and control measures are in place. The team conducts thorough reviews, analysis and testing to confirm the appropriate security and data controls (whether through technology, process, or behaviour) and the secure operation of the FCA systems and data are in place Role responsibilities Lead the FCA's Data Security Assurance Framework, ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, availability and appropriate use of corporate data, aligned to the FCA's Cyber Risk Management Framework, regulatory, legislative and internal control requirements Establish and deliver risk-based data security assurance across the FCA's data estate, including M365 security and compliance, cloud platforms, data lakes, AI systems and data repositories, ensuring the identification, assessment and treatment of security and data risks in line with the FCA's Cyber Risk Management Framework and associated tooling Drive the strategic evolution of the FCAs data security posture management for AI, assessing and assuring technical controls, data exposure and appropriate use across emerging AI capabilities such as MS Co-pilot, Agentic AI and AI-enabled platforms, ensuring security by design, effective data security governance and continuous assurance as the FCAs AI estate evolves Produce meaningful KPIs, KRIs, risk assessments and management information to support senior management decision-making, alignment with the FCA's Cyber Risk Management Framework and effective second-line Risk and Compliance oversight, while leading issue identification, remediation tracking and validation of corrective actions Lead and develop the FCA's Data Security Assurance capability, working across technology, cyber security, risk, compliance and data governance teams to embed effective controls throughout the data lifecycle, integrate assurance into the wider cyber risk management ecosystem and support consistent risk reporting, governance and oversight. Skills required Minimum: Proven experience leading a data security, cyber security, information security or assurance capability within a complex organisation, including building, developing and maturing teams, operating models and security capabilities Demonstrable experience designing, implementing and assuring data security controls and frameworks across SaaS, cloud and enterprise environments, aligned to recognised frameworks such as NIST CSF and ISO 27001 Strong understanding of data security principles and risks, including data discovery, data lineage, encryption, logging, access control, identity management, data loss prevention and protection against data exposure and exfiltration Essential: Experience delivering security assurance and risk assessments across applications, cloud platforms, data repositories, AI systems and broader technology environments, supported by continuous monitoring, control health reviews and risk reporting Experience establishing governance, assurance and control oversight processes, including attestations, control validation, remediation tracking and risk-based prioritisation Strong expertise in Microsoft Purview and Microsoft 365 security and compliance capabilities, including data discovery, classification, sensitivity labelling, DLP, Insider Risk Management, DSPM for AI and related E5 functionality Knowledge of regulatory, legal and compliance requirements relevant to data security and experience translating these into practical controls, assurance activities and risk management outcomes Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across technology, cyber security, data governance and business teams and to communicate complex security risks and control issues to senior leadership and executive stakeholders Experience integrating security tooling, telemetry, APIs and automation to improve assurance, risk visibility and control effectiveness across Microsoft, AWS and interconnected technology platforms Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with experience developing data security roadmaps, identifying emerging risks and driving improvements that strengthen organisational security posture Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Hybrid model where colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better regulation. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). The Cryptoassets and Technology Policy Team leads the development of the FCA’s policy solutions on cryptoassets. As digital technology and cryptoassets market develop and evolve, regulators need to innovate and adapt our regulatory framework to deal with new and evolving opportunities and risks. We are designing a more comprehensive regulatory framework for cryptoassets to help shape the future of this diverse, fast-paced and ever-changing sector. Cryptoassets and associated activities are due to be phased into the FCA’s perimeter. Our work includes the development, consultation and implementation of cryptoasset policy for retail consumers. You will be a key member of the team, shaping creative and evidence-based policy solutions that benefit consumers, markets and competition. Role responsibilities As a Senior Policy Advisor, you will own key cryptoasset policy issues by taking the lead in shaping proposals, reviewing information and collaborating with teams across the FCA You will drive impactful change by drafting public consultations on FCA rules and guidance, ensuring our priorities influence industry and regulatory developments Engage with stakeholders by building strong relationships with government, other regulators and industry participants to help shape the future of cryptoasset and related technology policy You will provide insight by delivering advice and briefings on cryptoasset and related technology policy issues to colleagues and senior management, shaping strategic outcomes You will grow your expertise on cryptoasset and related technology regulations that affect every aspect of consumer and business financial lives You will be part of transformation by playing a key role in a major regulatory change project, supporting the team and contributing to innovative solutions in an evolving policy landscape Skills required Minimum: Prior experience of policy analysis and development Prior experience presenting key issues clearly and succinctly both orally and in writing with public and private sector audience Prior experience of building and managing relationships with stakeholders Essential: Experience of analysing information item.title: Critical Third Parties Oversight Manager
item.description: Job title: Critical Third Parties Oversight Manager Division: Supervision, Policy and Competition Department: Critical Third Parties Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £67,100 to £100,000 and London £79,300 to £120,000 per annum (Salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Manager, Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Shafika via Shafika.shaikh@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Iona via Iona.magee@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. SPC oversees firms and individuals (supervision), creates and reviews the rules by which they operate (policy) and identifies and remedies ineffective competition in markets (competition). Under FSMA 2023, the FCA has taken on joint responsibility with PRA and the Bank of England for overseeing the operational resilience of CTPs. This is an extremely high profile area of work that is central to the FCA’s work to instil trust in financial services and minimise the impact of operational disruptions on the financial services industry. Role responsibilities Provide leadership to a team of FCA supervisors and operational resilience specialists in delivering the regulators’ joint oversight approach to Critical Third Parties and the services they provide to the FS sector Lead meetings with senior executives from CTPs on the resilience of their services Play a key role in the Technology, Resilience and Cyber Department’s leadership team, contributing to the delivery of the departmental strategy as we deliver on the FCA's agenda to protect consumers and markets from harm Work closely with a range of external stakeholders, including across HM Treasury, the Bank of England, PRA and National Cyber Security Centre and international regulators, on issues to do with systemic risk During live incidents affecting a firm, CTP or sector, be on call to respond out of hours and provide specialist input to the FCA's response Skills required Minimum: Demonstrable people management skills, evidence of coaching, motivating and leading a diverse team of people Prior experience of developing and delivering strategies to mitigate the risk of harm posed by firms’ business models and culture Prior extensive qualitative and quantitative analytical experience Essential: Good stakeholder management skills – ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders Good communication skills, both written and oral (ability to convey complex issues in a coherent and compelling way, including for communicating technical issues to non-technical audiences) Exceptionally good judgement, supported by highly developed reasoning skills and high levels of diligence; can demonstrate making challenging, risk-based choices in a complex and changing landscape Highly organised and experienced in managing a range of work across multiple firms/CTPs at the same time, prioritising appropriately and escalating where necessary Experience in dealing with contentious issues, taking decisive action and delivering difficult messages An ability to get up to speed on new issues quickly and innovative thinking for how to deal with new complex problems most effectively Significant experience working with either financial services firms, large third party providers (e.g. cloud service providers), across regulators and/or government departments Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page . Our values and culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer , and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timelines Advert Close Date: 10th September CV Review/Shortlist: 14th September First Interview: W/C 18th September Manager Assessment: W/C 28th September Second Interview: W/C 2nd October Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time. SC Clearance is required for this role ( SC Guidance ) - you will hold or will be required to obtain Security Check (SC) level vetting
