item.title: Security Control Room Officer in Security Operations - Debden Site
item.description: Location : Debden, Essex Department Overview The Security Operations team sits within the Bank of England’s Security Division and plays a vital role in protecting our people, tenants, visitors, buildings, assets and information. As part of the UK’s Critical National Infrastructure, and with responsibility for supporting the production of all Bank of England banknotes, our security environment is high-profile, complex and closely connected with law enforcement. This is an interesting and varied opportunity to join an organised, disciplined and professional team at the heart of the UK’s central bank. The Security Operations team is structured to provide flexibility, enabling colleagues to train, test and exercise while continuing to deliver essential day-to-day security operations. The team works closely with stakeholders across all business areas, making this a broad and engaging role in a unique security environment. Job Description As a Control Room Operator, you will work under the direction of the Security Control Room Shift Leader to help protect the Bank from internal and external physical security threats and support responses to infrastructure failures in partnership with others. This is a 24/7 operational role, working on a rotational shift pattern. The role focuses on overseeing IDS and CCTV systems, managing key communication activity and applying Bank-specific knowledge to support security requirements across different business areas. You will make security decisions in line with standard operating procedures, with support from senior colleagues where needed, and may occasionally direct contractor staff. Role Responsibilites As a Security Control Room Operator, you will play a key role in helping to protect the Bank of England’s people, buildings, assets and information. Working as part of a 24/7 security operation, your main responsibility will be to monitor and respond to physical security risks, internal incidents and infrastructure failures, using established procedures and the support of senior colleagues where needed. You will oversee key security systems including CCTV, alarms and other monitoring equipment, assess and escalate potential threats, and coordinate effective responses to a range of situations. These may include suspicious activity, protests, bomb warnings, crime, fire, flood, first aid incidents, security breaches and other emergencies. A typical shift may involve; control room duties, static guarding, patrolling, searching, visitor management, emergency response, mail examination, building protection, alarm monitoring, CCTV surveillance and asset protection. You will also take part in regular training, development and exercising activity to help maintain a high standard of operational readiness. This is a varied and responsible role that requires sound judgement, clear communication, strong attention to detail and the ability to remain calm under pressure. You will work closely with security colleagues, teams across the Bank, contractors and, when required, external emergency services to support a safe and secure environment. You will be required to work shifts which is predominantly a 3 on / 3 off rotation, but with two additional training days per month. This is a combination of early, late and night shifts on a rotation system. Hours of working are approximately 9 hours per shift and for training days. Role Requirements Minimum Criteria Proven experience working in the security industry, a control room environment, or a high-security site. Demonstrable experience using security systems such as CCTV, alarm systems and/or fire systems. Able to work a 24/7 rotational shift pattern, including early, late and night shifts. Able to communicate clearly and professionally, both verbally and in writing, including recording incidents and actions accurately. Essential Criteria Demonstrates sound judgement, integrity and professionalism when handling security-related matters. Able to remain calm, focused and effective when responding to incidents, alarms, emergency situations or competing priorities. Demonstrates good customer focus and the ability to provide a professional service to staff, visitors, contractors and stakeholders. Able to plan, prioritise and coordinate resources or activities effectively in response to operational requirements. Able to follow standard operating procedures and escalate security incidents appropriately when required. Demonstrates flexibility and reliability in supporting a shift-based operational environment. Desirable Criteria Holds a valid SIA Licence, security qualification or equivalent relevant qualification. Experience delivering a professional customer experience in a security, front-of-house, control room or operational environment. Experience supporting incident response, emergency procedures, access control, searching, patrolling or visitor management a Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information This role offers a salary of £28,640 and an annual, non-pensionable shift allowance of £8,000. In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two stages. This role closes for applications on 11 September 2026. Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Maintenance Technician in Property, Central Operations - London Sites
item.description: Location: London Sites Overview The Bank of England is the UK’s central bank, with a mission to promote the good of the people of the United Kingdom by maintaining monetary and financial stability. Our Property department plays a key role in supporting that mission by keeping the Bank’s buildings safe, operational and effective for colleagues across a complex, high-profile estate. About the role As an Engineering Shift Technician in Infrastructure Engineering, you’ll help maintain the critical building systems that support the Bank’s 24/7 operations. This hands-on role covers planned, preventative and reactive maintenance across critical, essential and non-essential systems, where reliability, safety, service and professionalism are central to everything we do. Key responsibilities Deliver planned, preventative and reactive maintenance through Planon IWMS, including accurate and timely updates via handheld HMI devices. Carry out daily and periodic checks, routine maintenance and statutory testing across HVAC, BMS, electrical, public health, fire, life safety, critical assets and other building engineering systems. Respond to engineering faults and failures in line with priority response and fix times, helping maintain safe environments and minimise disruption to the Bank’s operations. Support specialist OEM contractors with planned maintenance, reactive tasks and emergency call-outs. Provide accurate data for daily shift handover logs, reports, incident management and recovery exercises. Act as, or support, an Authorised Person for LV electrical and/or mechanical systems, working within Safe Systems of Work to support 24/7 operations. Champion health and safety, ensuring work is delivered in line with agreed methods, risk assessments, service levels and customer service standards. Contribute to the Bank’s collaborative, continuous improvement culture by sharing ideas, innovation and practical improvements. Participate in the weekly on-call technical support rota to support incident response, if required. About you Role Requirements Minimum criteria City & Guilds Level 3, or equivalent transferable qualification, in a relevant engineering discipline. IOSH Operating Safely qualification. Experience using IWMS planned and reactive maintenance tools, including handheld HMI devices. Experience operating and maintaining HVAC, BMS, electrical, public health and life safety systems. Demonstrable Authorised Person experience in HV or LV system operation, with experience working within defined Safe Systems of Work. Knowledge of statutory and compliance obligations relevant to engineering systems. Ability to follow Standard Operating Procedures and Emergency Operating Procedures, and read complex mechanical, electrical, control and public health drawings. Essential criteria Proven understanding of building services and maintenance risk management. Experience producing clear reports and tailored communications. Track record of applying procedures to support decisions and improvements. Practical experience collaborating to deliver agreed outcomes. Successful delivery of quality work, customer service and maintenance outcomes. Experience prioritising workloads and remaining resilient under pressure. Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed. From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information The salary for this role is £32,220. In addition, we also offer 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits We also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time. A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool. 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. Private medical insurance and income protection. National Security Vetting Process Employment in this role will be subject to the National Security Vetting clearance process (and typically can take between 6 to 12 weeks post offer) and the passing of additional Bank security checks in accordance with the Bank policy. Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice . The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis. The Application Process Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process. The assessment process will comprise of two stages. This role closes for applications on 11 September 2026 Please apply online, ensuring that you complete your work history and answer ALL the application questions fully and in detail as your application will not be considered if all mandatory questions are not fully completed.

item.title: Cyber Analyst in CYBER DEFENCE CENTRE
item.description: Cyber Analyst, Technology Directorate Permanent Full Time Leeds or London The Cyber Defence Centre (CDC) is responsible for detecting and responding to cyber-attacks against the Bank of England. Whilst the team is primarily located in the Bank's London office in Threadneedle Street, the team does also have a presence in the Leeds office. This posting is therefore open to London OR Leeds applicants. Department overview: Within the Cyber Security Division you will be working with people who are passionate about protecting the security and stability of our Technology estate. Whether it is identifying threats, uncovering vulnerabilities or ensuring robust and resilient infrastructure, you’ll be working at the cutting edge in a security-centric organisation. You’ll focus on ensuring security by design, and ensuring we have safe, stable and resilient systems. Collaborating closely with colleagues across Technology and throughout the organisation you will help the division safeguard critical systems and information. Our award-winning specialist teams are committed to developing their expertise in a constantly evolving environment. Aligned to industry best-practice, staff are encouraged to develop their skills both internally and externally, through mentoring, training and formal qualifications. Job description The Cyber Defence Centre (CDC) is responsible for detecting and responding to cyber-attacks against the Bank of England. The CDC is made up of four key domains: Capability, Threat, Detection Engineering and Defence Operations. Reporting to the Cyber Defence Operations Lead Operations lead in the Cyber Defence Operations (CDO) function, The successful candidate will take part in the operations rota ensuring security alerts are thoroughly investigated, escalated appropriately and take part in subsequent Cyber Security incident response activities as part of the wider Cyber Security incident response team where required. When not responding to security alerts or incidents, as part of the CDO function, the role holder will be expected to proactively seek opportunities to improve the team’s operational capability for both detection and response processes through a greater use of automation. The role will require close collaboration across all of the CDC’s core functions and has varied and challenging day-to-day responsibilities, as well as exposure to a range of cutting-edge technology in cyber security, data analytics and cyber threat intelligence. Key Experience / Skills Minimum: Good understanding of best practice security incident response concepts and approaches Practical experience in technical cyber security incident response methodologies Excellent written and verbal communication skills Essential: Experience working in Security Operations Centre with specific experience triaging security alerts and an understanding of wider cyber security incident response practices. Knowledge of computer network fundamentals, including network protocols and infrastructure (packet capture analysis, firewalls, web proxies, DNS etc.) Ability to convey complex information in a clear and concise manner Ability and willingness to learn new technical cyber security skills Logical mind-set Desirable: Experience developing and documenting incident response processes and designing IR playbooks. GCIH or similar qualification in Security Incident response The ability to acquire DV clearance (To be eligible to apply you must be a British citizen (either born here or naturalised) and one of your parents must be a British citizen or have substantial ties to the UK. Understanding of common cyber threats and attacker tactics, techniques and procedures and an ability to identify appropriate mitigation strategies Experience using automation or SOAR platforms Knowledge of incident response principles Experience using MITRE ATT&CK Experience using Splunk Experience using an intelligence platform Software development, scripting or programming skills Our Approach to Inclusion The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team. Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme . If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application. Salary and Benefits Information We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate. Leeds: £40,320 - £45,360 London: £44,800 - £50,400 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below: Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. item.title: Senior Manager, Business Manager, Office of CIO in TECHNOLOGY
item.description: Senior Manager, Business Manager, Office of CIO in Technology Directorate Permanent Full Time Leeds or London Part of the Bank’s Technology Leadership Team and reporting to the Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Central Services COO, this role provides the business management, governance and operational oversight needed to run safe, secure and resilient technology services for the Bank of England. As a member of the Technology Leadership Team, you will be individually and collectively responsible for the Bank’s information technology and computer systems, through which the Bank delivers its mission. You will lead the core OCIO disciplines that enable effective technology leadership, including financial management and reporting, strategic supplier management, resource and demand management, regulatory compliance, audit coordination, risk management and performance reporting. Core to your role will be building strong relationships with the CIO, the TLT and key partners across the Bank who work closely with the Technology Directorate, including Finance, Change and Planning, People, Risk, Procurement and other central functions. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. This will include setting clear goals and smart stretching objectives that are aligned to those of the team, division and directorate. You will also be responsible for managing all staff-related matters that may arise including performance, absence and sickness. Primary accountabilities Management of finances, performance and financial reporting • You are responsible for maintaining oversight of the financial performance of the Technology Directorate. • You work with the finance business partner and CIO to support financial and business planning, including the setting of budgets. • You define and monitor key financial, operational and supplier performance metrics, using data and insight to support prioritisation, investment decisions and transparent reporting to senior governance forums. • You are responsible for the provision of accurate and timely financial information to the CIO and to Court. Strategic supplier management • You maintain oversight of the Technology Directorate’s strategic supplier management approach, ensuring key supplier relationships are aligned to technology priorities, service resilience, commercial value and the Bank’s risk appetite. • You oversee the use of supplier segmentation, account management plans, performance scorecards and relationship reviews to ensure strategic suppliers are managed according to their criticality, value and risk profile. • You monitor strategic supplier performance, contractual obligations, service levels, key risks, improvement actions and value delivery, ensuring issues are escalated through the appropriate governance forums. • You support executive engagement with strategic suppliers, helping the Technology Leadership Team move supplier relationships beyond tactical renewals towards long-term partnership, innovation, resilience and continuous improvement. • You ensure supplier insight, market intelligence and third-party risk information are used to inform technology planning, investment decisions, commercial pipelines and future sourcing strategies Internal process management • You maintain oversight of internal business processes that support Technology Directorate productivity, service quality, cost control and timely delivery. • You evaluate existing business processes, determining and outlining business process improvements. • You work with the Technology Leadership Team and other technology leaders to identify opportunities for innovation, automation, simplification and continuous improvement across Technology Directorate operations. • You work with the Change and Planning Directorate to oversee the implementation of Bank-wide business process improvement initiatives. Resource and demand management • You are responsible for maintaining oversight of overall headcount within the Technology Directorate to ensure the directorate operates within its headcount budget. • You support the capacity planning process as part of the budgeting and forecasting cycle, ensuring workforce plans are aligned to technology priorities, delivery commitments and affordability. • You work with the Change and Planning Directorate to ensure that change programmes are resourced appropriately. Regulatory compliance • You are responsible for ensuring the Technology Directorate complies with external regulatory requirements and internal policies, including public procurement policy, technology resilience obligations and compliance relating to Critical National Infrastructure. • You coordinate the gathering of internal information in response to regulatory requests. • You collaborate within the directorate and with partners across the Bank to foster a culture of compliance. Risk and audit management • You establish, maintain and review the Technology Directorate’s risk management framework, mechanisms and tools, ensuring they support consistent identification, assessment, monitoring, control and reporting of technology risk. • You support and monitor the first line of defence in applying technology risk management tools, including identifying, assessing, monitoring and controlling technology risk, and advising on proportionate mitigation measures. • You assess the adequacy and effectiveness of controls from a technology risk perspective during due diligence of new products and applications, incident handling and material change activity, providing advice and recommendations where required. • You collaborate within the directorate and with partners across the Bank to foster a shared understanding of risk. • You work with the TLT to support the management of Technology risks and controls. • You support the management of technology audit activity by coordinating evidence, tracking actions, monitoring closure of agreed mitigations and ensuring issues are escalated through the appropriate governance forums. • You coordinate the gathering of internal information in response to audit requests, ensuring responses are complete, timely and aligned with agreed ownership of audit actions. Team management and management of PS/PA office • You are accountable for building knowledge, skills and best practice within your teams and across the Technology Directorate. • You are responsible for developing and mentoring a high-performing team of direct reports. Role requirements Minimum/Essential criteria • Proven experience and track record of building relationships across business units and with a range of stakeholders, balancing competing interests and generating a collaborative, one-team mindset. • Successful leadership experience, established over several years, within a high-performing central operations or COO team, or in a comparable technology business management function. • Established understanding of finance, budgeting and forecasting, with an accounting qualification desirable, and experience using financial insight to support technology investment, supplier and workforce decisions. • Established understanding of regulatory compliance, audit management and risk management in a complex technology or regulated environment. • Established understanding of internal process management and capacity and demand planning. Strong stakeholder management and interpersonal skills • You have very strong interpersonal skills at senior levels and a proven ability to influence decisions across organisational boundaries. • You are an effective communicator, able to create a compelling narrative and inspire people to follow you. • You can build trusted relationships at all levels of the Bank, enabling you to have difficult conversations in pursuit of a common objective. You can make and recommend difficult decisions. • You are recognised as an empathetic people leader and a role model for the Bank’s leadership values, promoting an inclusive culture and working environment. An experienced ‘operator’ within a central operations team • You are an experienced technology business management operator, using financial, workforce, supplier and performance insight to influence the directorate’s budgeting and forecasting process and support delivery within agreed budgets. • You are an experienced capacity and demand planner, able to make and support recommendations about the directorate’s workforce while balancing stakeholder needs and understanding due process. • You have demonstrable understanding of regulatory compliance within a comparable organisation. • You have demonstrable understanding of risk management processes within a comparable organisation. An ambassador for the Bank • You are able to build and tap into a wide external network to learn, attract talent, and help drive the reputation of the Bank. You might represent the Bank at relevant external engagements. This is a people management role. You will be responsible for day to day management of the team and for defining roles and responsibilities. You will develop your team through sharing information effectively, coaching and communicating a clear vision to ensure that your staff are productive, engaged and motivated to deliver the area's aims. item.title: AI Analyst
item.description: Job Title: AI Analyst Division: Data, Technology and Innovation Department: AI Product Development Salary: National (Edinburgh and Leeds) ranging from £53,800 to £72,000 and London from £59,200 to £80,000 per annum (salary offered will be based on skills and experience) This role is graded as: Senior Associate – Regulatory Your external recruitment contact is Benjamin via benjamin.paulon@fca.org.uk Your internal recruitment contact is Pat via Patrycja.Matachowska@fca.org.uk Applications must be submitted through our online portal. Applications sent via social media or email will not be accepted. About the FCA and team We regulate financial services firms in the UK, to keep financial markets fair, thriving and effective. By joining us, you’ll play a key part in protecting consumers, driving economic growth, and shaping the future of UK finance services. The Data, Technology and Innovation (DTI) division enables the FCA to be a digital-first, data-led smart regulator by delivering a secure, agile, and cost-effective technology and data ecosystem that drives better decisions, transparency, and operational efficiency. Sitting within DTI, the AI Product Development department scopes and shapes AI solutions across the FCA and helps manage the organisation-wide pipeline of AI initiatives, ensuring work is prioritised, well-defined and aligned to strategic outcomes. Role responsibilities Identify and shape high value opportunities for applying AI across the organisation, enabling smarter and more effective regulatory outcomes to maximise impact Facilitate structured discovery workshops with stakeholders to surface pain points, map processes and pinpoint where AI can deliver meaningful improvements that increase efficiency Build credibility and influence at all levels of the organisation, including senior leaders and decision-makers, adapting communication style and messages to suit different audiences and securing buy-in for AI-driven change and innovation initiatives Translate business challenges into clear functional and non-functional requirements, working collaboratively with technical teams to design AI enabled solutions that meet real needs Manage and prioritise a pipeline of AI initiatives, partnering with data scientists and leadership to focus effort on the highest impact projects for maximum value Contribute to the organisation’s wider AI adoption strategy through insight, stakeholder engagement, and evidence-based recommendations to guide direction Advocate best practice in business analysis, promoting consistency, quality and knowledge sharing across the department to develop capability Gain experience delivering experimental and innovative projects that address real world challenges such as financial crime and consumer protection to create tangible outcomes Build a distinctive skill set at the intersection of AI, data, technology and regulation within a collaborative, learning focused environment to support career growth Skills required Minimum: Experience in a senior business analyst role or a comparable position such as Consultant, Solution/Service Designer or Product Owner Experience delivering projects across the full lifecycle, using both waterfall and agile methodologies Working knowledge of artificial intelligence, including areas such as large language models (LLMs), agentic AI, and prompt engineering. Essential: Solid understanding of core Business Analysis techniques, including user journey mapping, process mapping, requirements gathering and the ability to design and facilitate collaborative workshops Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the confidence and credibility to engage, challenge and gain buy-in from senior leaders and subject matter experts across the organisation Ability to work through complex problems, identifying underlying issues and opportunities for improvement Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to adapt style, language and level of detail to different audiences, from technical specialists to senior executives, ensuring complex concepts are understood and acted upon Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to adapt style, language and level of detail to different audiences, from technical specialists to senior executives, ensuring complex concepts are understood and acted upon Experience navigating complex stakeholder environments, balancing competing priorities and influencing decisions with minimal supervision Benefits 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Colleagues spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office each month (60% for Directors and Executive Directors) across our London, Leeds and Edinburgh offices Non-contributory pension (8–12% depending on age) and life assurance at eight times your salary Private healthcare with Bupa, income protection, and 24/7 Employee Assistance 35 hours of paid volunteering annually A flexible benefits scheme designed around your lifestyle For a full list of our benefits, and our recruitment process as a whole visit our benefits page. Our values & culture Our colleagues are the key to our success as a regulator. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive culture: one that’s free from discrimination and bias, celebrates difference, and supports colleagues to deliver at their best. We believe that our differences and similarities enable us to be a better organisation – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation, and delivers better regulation. If you require any adjustments due to a disability or condition, your recruiter is here to help - reach out for tailored support. We welcome diverse working styles and aim to find flexible solutions that suit both the role and individual needs, including options like part-time and job sharing where applicable. Disability Confident: our hiring approach We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer, and therefore, people or individuals with disabilities and long-term conditions who best meet the minimum criteria for a role will go through to the next stage of the recruitment process. In cases of high application volumes, we may progress applicants whose experience most closely matches the role’s key requirements. Useful information and timeline Advert Closing: 6th September at 11:59pm CV Review/Shortlist: 14th September Interview W/C: 21st September Your Recruiter will discuss the process in detail with you during screening for the role, therefore, please make them aware if you are going to be unavailable for any date during this time
